# dsh-app-usage

Local session statistics with a per-provider breakdown (activity heatmap panel).

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin,
packaged as a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and
`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `app-usage` row into the active profile.
The client half is served from `lib/client.js` (`dsh.client.platform: web`).

## Install

- Desktop app: **Plugins** → install `github:bosenok/dsh-app-usage` (private repository:
  give the machine git access), then enable the bundle.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:bosenok/dsh-app-usage`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh-app-usage`.

Enabling the bundle mounts the plugin; HMR applies it to a running app, and a
restart makes sure the client half is rebuilt.

> Note for the app-managed `desktop` profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`
> only installs the dependency and copies the package; unlike a regular profile
> it does not enable the bundle. Enable it by adding the package name to
> `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` (or through the
> Plugins page). Other profiles enable the installed bundle automatically.


## Development

`lib/` is built and committed; the sources live in `src/`. Rebuild the client with
the repository's Vite config (`npx vite build` → `dist/`, then the wrapper in
`build/wrapper.js` produces `lib/client.js`).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code bundled into `lib/` and its
licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

plugins.description: Side chat for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI: fork the current session into an ephemeral conversation that can really edit files, without polluting the main transcript.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-side-chat

A **side chat** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI: open the right sidebar from the session header, add the **Side chat** (「侧边会话」) tab, and keep the main conversation untouched — while the side conversation still carries the same agent, the same tools, and **really edits the same workspace files**.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![CI](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/flyer103/dsh-side-chat)](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat/releases)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@flyer103/dsh-side-chat)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flyer103/dsh-side-chat)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## Quick start

```bash
# npm (recommended)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @flyer103/dsh-side-chat

# GitHub, default branch or a pinned tag
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:flyer103/dsh-side-chat
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:flyer103/dsh-side-chat#v0.6.0

# local checkout (records a link: dependency)
cd /path/to/dsh-side-chat
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "$(pwd)"

# tarball built with `npm pack`
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/flyer103-dsh-side-chat-0.6.0.tgz
```

Use the profile you actually run: `desktop` for the Desktop app, `web` for a web profile. Prefer quitting the Desktop app before installing into `desktop` (the CLI waits on the profile write lock) and reopen it afterwards; either way a restart is required. `add` also appends the bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`; you do not edit the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand. Re-running is safe.

Alternatively, from a local checkout:

```bash
node scripts/install.mjs --profile desktop            # idempotent; never restarts DSH
node scripts/install.mjs --profile desktop --dry-run  # show the plan only
```

Then **restart DSH**, open a session, and expand the right sidebar from the session header (**「Open sidebar」** / 「打开侧边栏」). On the sidebar's guide page, click the **「Side chat」** (「侧边会话」) card; the side chat opens as a native tab in that column. (There is no session-header side-chat button and no floating overlay — the entry lives in the right sidebar, also reachable from the tab strip's add control; inside an open side-chat tab, the status bar's **New side chat** button opens another one.) Send the first message: that tab's side chat is created on that send and destroyed when you close its tab. Every click of the guide card, and every press of a tab's **New side chat** button, opens another side-chat tab in the same pane, each with its own side session and a chip numbered within the parent session (**Side chat**, **Side chat 2**, …; 「侧边会话」, 「侧边会话 2」…). Collapsing the sidebar or switching to another tab only pauses a side chat; opening a tab without sending costs nothing. Closing one side-chat tab destroys only that side chat — the other side chats and the main session are unaffected.

## What it does

- **Native sidebar tab** — lives in the session's right sidebar next to the other tabs; no standalone session-header button and no floating overlay.
- **Several at once** — a parent session can hold multiple independent side-chat tabs, each its own ephemeral side session with a numbered chip; open another from the guide card or from a tab's **New side chat** button.
- **Inherits context** — the parent's completed turns plus a snapshot of what the main session is doing right now, taken when that side chat is created.
- **Inherits the agent** — same working directory, preset composition, tools, skills, model routing, sandbox mode and approval policy.
- **Really edits files** — write/edit/bash changes land in the same workspace and the main session sees them.
- **Isolates the transcript** — side-chat turns never appear in the main conversation, the session list, or the subagent catalog.
- **Streams the reply** — assistant text, reasoning and tool calls render token by token from a live event stream while the turn runs; when the transport cannot stream, the tab falls back to polling.
- **Shows its own usage** — a slim dock under the composer (the same spot as DSH's main composer dock) shows this side chat's total tokens, cache-hit percentage, and a small context-occupancy ring + percentage. Hover for the exact uncached-input, cache-read and output counts (plus a cache-write count when the provider reports one) and the approximate `~used / window` pair. The dock starts hidden until the side chat has a usage sample, and it resets with each new side session.
- **Destroys on close** — closing a tab disposes that tab's side chat and the host tries to remove its persisted artifact; a closed side chat cannot be reopened, and the other side chats and the main session are unaffected. Collapsing the sidebar or switching tabs only pauses it.

## Compatibility

- DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (Desktop profile, Web GUI) — the tested target. This release was verified against a real `dsh web` process in an isolated DSH home with a fresh `web` profile: the plugin launches, all eight host routes answer (including the SSE route's JSON fallback), and the client bundle is served.
- No `engines.dsh` and no DSH peer dependency are declared, so DSH does not version-gate installation. That is separate from the tested version: newer DSH releases are untested.
- Web platform only (`dsh.client.platform: web`); no CLI/TUI surface.
- Node.js `>= 22`; the plugin itself is dependency-free ESM with no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports.
- UI copy follows the DSH language setting (Settings → General → Language): Chinese and English are built in, and any other language falls back to English. Technical details — host error messages, routes, event and tool names — stay in English.

## Known limitations

- Approval prompts are not shown inside the side-chat tab: the side session inherits the parent's approval policy, and if that policy asks a human, the side session waits. Use a non-interactive policy (for example `danger-full-access`) for side chats that must write files.
- A closed tab cannot be restored: reopening the guide card or pressing **New side chat** starts a new side chat, whose agent is created on the next message.
- P1, designed but not implemented: model picker, surviving a GUI restart, approval rendering in the tab.
- The inherited context is a snapshot taken when that side chat is created; later main-session turns are not pushed into an existing side chat, and each side chat keeps its own snapshot.
- Token streaming rides on a streamable `fetch` response. If the page transport buffers the response (detected by a missing first frame), the tab falls back to snapshot polling: the running indicator returns and the reply still appears while it grows, at poll granularity.
- Each side chat's first request is roughly as large as the parent's next request (it carries the inherited history), so N concurrent side chats multiply that first-request cost.
- The usage dock is approximate and side-scoped: its token totals and cache-hit percentage cover what this side chat itself billed — its own requests, including the inherited context its first request re-sends — and never the parent's earlier requests; its context percentage is absolute for the same reason, and it omits DSH's projected-token correction, so it can trail the main composer's context bar by up to one step. It shows no turns, steps or tok/s, has no click-open dialogs, and cannot follow DSH's Performance & usage detailed/compact preference; its content is fixed.
- A reattached side-chat tab whose session log exceeds the 2000-entry snapshot page can undercount earlier usage in that dock. A tab that has watched the side chat since its first message is unaffected, because every committed event reaches it.

## Documentation

- [docs/USAGE.md](docs/USAGE.md) — full semantics: inheritance, isolation, mutation, lifecycle, installation, rollback, troubleshooting.
- [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) — scope, phases and adversarial notes.
- [docs/CONTRACT.md](docs/CONTRACT.md)

plugins.description: In-conversation workflow run timeline for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workflow-ui

[![CI](https://github.com/zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

DeepSeek Harness Web GUI 的对话内工作流运行时间线：把官方 `workflow` 工具卡与 `workflow-run` 聊天节点替换成横向时间线——轨道 + 阶段站 + 子代理药丸 + 循环弧线 + 并行带，且**开跑之前就能看到全部计划**。

English documentation in [README.en.md](README.en.md)。

![dsh-workflow-ui 截图](docs/screenshot.png)

窄窗口自动换行（同排弧 + ↩ 回边徽标）：

![dsh-workflow-ui 换行模式](docs/screenshot-wrap.png)

## 功能

- **对话内嵌卡片** — 每次 workflow 运行一张卡，长在对话流里，无需打开任何面板。
- **计划先行** — 客户端扫描 workflow 脚本（`phase()` 调用、`parallel()` 块、阶段回访），开跑前就渲染出全部计划站点、药丸占位与依赖弧线。
- **并行带** — `parallel()` 阶段渲染为抬升轨道，fork/merge 接头为圆角弧。
- **弧线** — 非相邻前向边与循环回边在轨道上空飞行：弧道按跨度分配（短跨低道、相交上推）、8px 圆角拐点、落地箭头；落入运行中站点的弧点亮为 march。宽屏画完整弧线；窄屏换行时只画同排弧，跨排回边由 `↩` 徽标承担。
- **药丸折叠** — 单站超过 5 个子代理自动折叠为「＋N」展开片；展开状态跨实时刷新保留；隐藏药丸里有运行中的会在折叠片上闪呼吸点。
- **药丸跳转子会话** — 点击药丸按 DSH 0.2.1 契约（`openSession({parentSessionId, childSessionId, mode})`，mode 传 `unknown` 由工作区自行解析）直达对应子会话；支持键盘聚焦与 Enter 触发。
- **自带 agent 预设** — 安装即向名册添加 `Workflow 编排` 预设（标准全量工具 + "多步任务主动用 workflow"的 persona 指引），卸载即移除。
- **DSH 官方图标** — StateDot 状态点（done/error = 6px 实心核，running = 中性 spinner 弧，pending = idle 点）、官方 ListPen 卡头图标、1px Check/Close 标记。
- **子代理药丸** — 逐 agent 状态 + 表情（运行中张望/眨眼），结算勾，未启动的计划占位。
- **主题与无障碍** — 经 DSH 别名 token 适配亮/暗主题，全链路尊重 `prefers-reduced-motion`，状态字形带 `aria` 标签。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui
```

安装后重启一次 dsh（组合变更），再刷新页面。要求 DSH `>=0.1.0-rc.5`；已在 `0.2.0-rc.2` 与 `0.2.1-rc.2` 实测，web profile。

装好后建议切换到自带的 **Workflow 编排** 预设（新会话选择器里），模型会对多步任务主动使用 workflow 编排。

## 原理

两个 keyed 槽位以 `priority: -1` 影子官方渲染器（官方默认 `0`，priority 最低者渲染；本组件崩溃会自动 abdicate 回退官方）：

- `conversation.chat.node` key `workflow-run` — 数据来自官方 Definition 对持久化事件（`tool-workflow/run-start|agent-start|agent-end|run-end`）的投影，本插件只换呈现。
- `tool.call.toolview` key `workflow` — 渲染不可见标记（该行经 CSS `:has` 隐藏，0.2.1 起连同 turn-process 流程头一并隐藏），并把工具入参的脚本元数据 stash 进模块 store，供运行卡做计划先行渲染。

样式以 `<style data-plugin>` 一次性注入、卸载时移除；类名全部 `zcf-` 前缀。颜色落在 14 个局部 `--color-*` token，映射到 DSH `--dsw-alias-*`。

## 开发

零依赖，Node >= 20。

```bash
npm run check     # 语法检查 + 单元测试 + 构建 + lib 检查 + 门面冒烟
npm run preview   # 生成 docs/preview/preview.html（亮/暗卡片）
```

无头截图预览：

```bash
chrome --headless=new --virtual-time-budget=3000 --screenshot=shot.png docs/preview/preview.html
```

布局常量参考 ZCode 的公开工作流呈现设计（站宽 168 / 间距 192 / 灯心 +17，弧基 26 / 道距 14，6–8px 圆角接头，120/160/200/320ms 运动 token）。状态点与图标复现 DSH 官方 `dsh-client-ui-primitives` 的形制（StateDot、ListPen、Check、Close）。本插件与 ZCode、DSH 官方均无隶属关系。

## 路线图

迭代方向与版本主题见 [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md)（下一版 v0.3.0：完成态折叠摘要 + 耗时/循环指标 + 失败复盘）。

## 边界说明

- 工具行只作为隐形数据源存在；时间线卡是会话中的唯一入口。
- 宽屏单排画完整弧线；换行模式只画同排弧，跨排依赖以 `↩` 徽标提示。
- 完成后卡片默认收成一行复盘摘要（阶段/进度/循环/失败定位/耗时，耗时需上游时间字段支持）；状态词为内置中文，locale 通道暂未接。
- 只读消费 workflow 事件，不保存任何平行编排状态。

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE) © zuiyouli

plugins.description: DSH 超大会话压缩插件：上下文实时监测（窗口×0.85）触发，分块摘要再合并，小会话仍走自带压缩
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-big-compact

**[中文](README.md) | [English](README.en.md)**

**超大会话压缩插件。** dsh 自带压缩（compaction-basic）会把要压缩的旧历史一次性塞进一个模型请求；会话涨到几 MB 之后，中转会拒绝（404 `model_not_found`），`/compact` 只剩一句 “Compaction could not produce a useful summary”。本插件在 `llm/stream` 瀑布上兜底：**只在压缩请求超过阈值时接管**，把它切成多块分别摘要、再合并成最终检查点；小会话与普通对话一律原样放行。

设计取向参考 [billion-context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context)：普通请求/小上下文不走它，只有大到本地压缩处理不了时才启用。

## 触发条件（实时监测）

1. 每次 `llm/stream` 都用 `ctx.tokenMeter.measure(session)` **实测该会话当前上下文 tokens**（上下文每轮都在变，按实测算）；
2. **窗口是动态的**：每次压缩请求先 `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)` 读模型声明的 `contextWindow`（例如 profile 里写 850000 → 安全线 850000 × 0.85 = 722500）；解析失败才退回配置/500k 兜底；
3. 实测值（拿不到时退回请求体估算）> **窗口 × 0.85** 就分块；
4. 另外保留 **请求体 > 4 MB** 的字节兜底（中转请求体上限）。

上下文占到 85% 时会打一行预告：`上下文实时监测：… tokens，已达窗口 … 的 95%，下次压缩将分块`。

## 工作方式

```
dsh 压缩引擎
  └─ ctx.llm.stream({ purpose: 'compaction', messages: [系统提示, 历史…, 压缩指令] })
       └─ [本插件] 先实测上下文 / 解析窗口，再决定
            ├─ 未超线 → next()，走 dsh 自带压缩（行为不变）
            └─ 超线   → 分块模式
                 1. 历史消息按时间顺序装箱（默认 1.5 MB/块）
                 2. 每块一个小请求 → 结构化要点（默认 max_tokens 6000，3 路并发）
                 3. 各块摘要合并；合并后仍超线就再做一轮
                 4. 合并摘要 + dsh 原始压缩指令发给模型，得到最终检查点
                 5. 按 raw chunk 协议回放（text 块 + finish stop）给压缩引擎落盘
```

- 子请求的 `purpose` 是 `compaction-chunk` / `compaction-final`，不会再次触发插件（无递归）。
- **空摘要算失败**：某块返回空或少于 10 字时，自动重试并把输出预算翻倍（最多 20000 tokens），仍失败则二分再试（最多 2 层）。
- 整条链路失败时回放 `finish{kind:'error'}`，`/compact` 会照常报错并写会话日志，不会静默。

## 配置

`/root/.big-compact/config.json`（不存在时用默认值）：

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `thresholdBytes` | 4000000 | 请求体超过该字节数才接管（字节兜底） |
| `maxContextTokens` | 0 | 0 = 按模型动态解析 `contextWindow`；>0 = 强制覆盖 |
| `contextFillRatio` | 0.85 | 实测上下文 > 模型窗口 × 该比例 就接管 |
| `chunkBytes` | 1500000 | 每块字节预算（UTF-8 字节） |
| `chunkMaxTokens` | 6000 | 每块摘要的 max_tokens（重试时翻倍，上限 20000） |
| `finalMaxTokens` | 8000 | 最终合并的 max_tokens |
| `concurrency` | 3 | 分块请求并发数 |
| `retries` | 2 | 单块失败重试次数 |
| `maxMessageChars` | 200000 | 单条消息最多保留字符数（防一个巨大工具结果吃掉整块） |
| `maxDepth` | 2 | 失败二分重试的最大深度 |
| `verbose` | true | 是否打印每块进度 |

## 日志

`/root/dsh-web.log` 里搜 `[big-compact]`：

```
[big-compact] 已启用：窗口 按模型动态解析，安全线 85%，分块 1.43 MB，并发 3
[big-compact] 上下文实时监测：6464308 tokens，已达窗口 850000 的 760%（安全线 85%），下次压缩将分块
[big-compact] 超大压缩请求（上下文 6464308 tokens（实测）> 窗口 850000 × 0.85 = 722500）→ 分块模式
[big-compact] 压缩请求 23.13 MB，切成 9 块
[big-compact] 分块 1/9 完成（1.43 MB → 3621 字）
...
[big-compact] 压缩完成：9 块，用时 96.6s，摘要 3586 字
```

## 测试

```bash
node test/unit.mjs          # 离线：分块、合并、拦截边界、空摘要重试、动态窗口、失败兜底
node test/live.mjs 12 3     # 真机联调：12 MB 合成压缩请求 → 分块 → 合并（直连中转）
```

## 安装 / 卸载

- 已注册进 `profiles/web/package.json`（依赖 + `dsh.profile.bundles`）并建立
  `node_modules/dsh-big-compact` 链接；**重启一次 web 生效**（`patchReload: startup`）。
- 卸载：从 `dependencies` 与 `dsh.profile.bundles` 删掉 `dsh-big-compact`，
  删 `node_modules/dsh-big-compact` 链接；重启 web。插件文件在 `/root/dsh-big-compact`。

## 已知限制

- 分块摘要是有损的：每块只保留要点，细节以原会话日志为准。
- 依赖中转能接受单块 1.5 MB 的请求；若某个中转更严格，把 `chunkBytes` 调小即可。
- 只处理 `purpose === 'compaction'` 的请求；普通对话不拦截。

plugins.description: 这是专门存插件代码的新仓库
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-sync

DSH 跨设备同步插件。通过**使用者自己的私有 HTTPS Git 仓库或 SFTP 服务器**同步会话、附件、配置及选定工程，支持在线安全范围应用、离线恢复及经确认的插件升级。

- 当前版本：**0.6.0**；许可证：MIT。
- 公开源码／安装包：https://github.com/vxdeus/dsh-sync
- 公开软件与私人备份完全分开：发布包不含作者的同步仓库、服务器连接信息、账号、密钥、令牌、会话、附件或工程数据。
- 首次安装没有预配置远端。安装、启动及打开面板不自动上传或下载；已有本机配置不会被安装初始化覆盖。

## 环境与安装

需要带插件管理器的 DeepSeek Harness，运行时 Node.js **24 或更高版本**。SFTP 另需本机可用的 OpenSSH `ssh` / `sftp`。在线应用及插件升级取决于宿主提供的接口；不可用时明确禁用，不会绕过授权或降级为直接覆盖会话文件。

在 DSH 插件管理器中安装 GitHub Release 的 `dsh-sync.tgz` 或带版本号安装包，并核对同一 Release 的 `SHA256SUMS`。随后**完全退出并重新打开 DSH**，再刷新原有网页。仅刷新网页不能保证更新宿主插件的模块缓存。

入口：**设置 → 跨机同步**，或侧边栏底部的**同步**。

## 配置自己的存储

配置文件位于当前 `DSH_HOME` 下的 `dsh-sync.json`；未设置 `DSH_HOME` 时为用户目录下的 `.dsh/dsh-sync.json`。它只留在本机，不进入同步快照。请在本机编辑，勿将真实配置提交到公开源码仓库或贴入聊天。

### 私有 HTTPS Git

新建仅自己／授权协作者可访问的私有数据仓库，使用独立同步分支。下面仅是**不可连接的占位示例**，请替换仓库和账号：

```json
{
  "backend": "gitee",
  "repoUrl": "https://git.example.invalid/your-account/private-sync.git",
  "branch": "dsh-sync",
  "username": "your-account",
  "token": "",
  "privateRepoConfirmed": false,
  "profiles": ["desktop"],
  "includeAttachments": true,
  "maxExtraBytes": 209715200,
  "extras": []
}
```

`gitee` 是保留的 Git 后端配置名，界面也沿用 Gitee 标签。Git 传输使用 HTTPS 用户名／令牌认证；不同提供商的兼容性和权限要求需自行验证。

令牌可只设置在本机环境变量 `DSH_SYNC_TOKEN`，或写入本机配置的 `token` 字段。使用最小必要仓库权限，不把凭据嵌入 URL。**亲自确认数据仓库为私有后**才将 `privateRepoConfirmed` 改为 `true`；这是本机确认声明，插件不会自动查询或更改远端可见性。

**不得将本项目的公开源码仓库作为个人同步目标。** 插件会拒绝此目标。切换仓库、分支或账号会隔离 Git 工作副本；更换旧设备配置后建议先下载核对，不强制推送覆盖远端。

### 自己的 SFTP 服务器

不提供托管服务器、共享账号、预置主机公钥或私钥。每台设备自行生成／保管密钥，并由服务器管理员授权设备公钥。在本机配置：

- `backend`：`sftp`。
- `sftp.host`：自己的服务器域名或地址；`port`：SSH 端口。
- `sftp.username`：自己获授权的服务器用户。
- `sftp.remoteRoot`：安全的 `/data/` 子目录，例如 `/data/my-sync`；须按服务器 **SFTP 可见路径**配置。
- `sftp.privateKeyPath`：本机私钥绝对路径，私钥不经过网页、不进入同步。
- `sftp.hostKey`：通过可信独立渠道核对的完整 `ssh-ed25519` 服务器公钥。不要关闭主机身份校验，也不要盲目信任首次网络扫描结果。

密钥需可用于非交互式 OpenSSH 认证。账户、密钥和目录访问权限由使用者管理。Git 和 SFTP 备份相互独立；切换存储不会搬运或删除旧备份。面板保存存储选择不会自动传输。

## 日常使用

### 源设备上传

1. 先检查状态与同步范围。工程／额外文件须手动添加自定义映射，例如逻辑名 `my-project`。
2. 可执行**本地预演**：它会扫描并暂存本机数据；已配置 Git 时还可能创建本地提交，**不是只读检查**，但不推送或访问远端。
3. 明确确认后上传。仅当显示远端回读／哈希核验成功时，才视为备份成功。超时后可能显示待确认，不自动重复推送。
4. 同一时刻只在一台设备编辑。不是实时双向同步，也不自动合并两台设备的分叉历史。

### 目标设备下载与恢复

1. 安装兼容版本插件，并配置自己的仓库凭据或 SFTP 授权。各设备按**相同逻辑名**映射工程，本机目标路径可以不同。
2. 默认在线模式只应用宿主允许的安全范围：冷历史通过原生接口导入；已加载、分叉、格式不支持的会话及忙碌工程保留，运行时配置等推迟应用。查看未应用项，不能将部分应用当成全量成功。
3. **仅下载／离线恢复**只产生暂存计划，不覆盖现有会话或工程。检查结果后完全退出 DSH，再运行该结果给出的恢复命令。需可运行 Node.js 24+；不要在另一台机器复用生成的本机恢复脚本。
4. 恢复核对源哈希及下载时的目标基线，覆盖前验证备份；冲突时停止，不自动改权限。内容相同的只读附件保持原样。失败计划不可重跑，先检查日志并重新下载。
5. 恢复中失败会尝试回滚，仍可能出现需人工处理的不完整回滚。请保留日志和备份；本插件不替代独立备份。

离线计划会记录本次宿主端口并检测监听，但仍须自行确认**所有相关 DSH 进程已退出**。不提供自动关机、自动关闭 DSH、配套桌面宿主补丁或一键授权新设备的功能。

下载尚未完整应用时会阻止后续上传，避免用旧本机快照覆盖远端。不要轻易勾选覆盖未应用远端内容；只有核对并明确接受丢弃风险后才能使用此选项。

### 跨设备插件升级

快照可携带已安装插件的精确版本、支持的本地安装包和升级说明。目标设备下载后仅检测差异；**用户选中具体插件并再次确认后**才交给宿主插件管理器安装。模型调用另需本次插件管理授权。

不自动批准依赖构建脚本，不自动降级，不自动重启。远端说明及本地插件包都属于不受信任输入，请先核对来源；安装插件意味着允许代码在宿主环境执行。若返回待重启，由使用者手动重启。安装后重新下载恢复计划，以免使用安装前的旧基线。

## 同步范围、隐私与限制

- 包含：指定 profile 的安装声明／锁文件、允许的会话与 `storages` / `state` 文件、`.agent-presets`、可选附件、已有 `dsh-pet` 配置和明确添加的自定义项。
- 不直接复制：`node_modules`、模型／OAuth 登录凭据、`integrations`、IM 聊天存储、运行时、缓存、同步配置、私钥和令牌。插件包按白名单另行归档，不直接归档 profile。
- 本机搜索覆盖诊断与额度预测缓存不跨机覆盖；真实费用账本与搜索用量日志仍在允许范围内。
- 默认排除工程依赖、Git 历史和构建产物。凭据路径过滤不能识别任意正文中的秘密。**会话、附件、插件配置、脚本和工程可能本来就包含隐私／密码；上传前自行审查。**
- 私人快照及默认 Git 提交可能记录设备主机名、系统用户名和配置账号，并非匿名同步。私有 Git / SSH 提供访问控制和传输保护，**不提供客户端端到端加密**。Git 历史可能保留已删除的内容；SFTP 历史快照和未引用对象暂不自动清理。
- 目录名及部分文本中的用户目录可做占位符转换；压缩历史内部路径和自定义工程内容不保证跨盘符自动修复。迁移后可能需重新定位工程。
- 单项自定义同步默认上限 200 MiB；缺失、超限或未映射项目可能阻止上传，避免静默丢失旧备份。
- IM 机器人历史不在同步范围内；同步 DSH 会话不等于两个 QQ 机器人自动续接话题。

## 模型工具

| 工具 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `dsh_sync_status` | 只读检查配置、范围及插件升级提醒 |
| `dsh_sync_extras` | 添加／移除／查看本机工程映射，不传输 |
| `dsh_sync_upload` | 明确要求后上传；`dryRun: true` 本地预演 |
| `dsh_sync_download` | `mode: online` 安全在线范围；`mode: offline` 下载并生成离线计划 |
| `dsh_sync_update_plugins` | 仅安装用户明确确认的当前计划中所选插件 |

## 开发与发布

```sh
node scripts/test.mjs
node scripts/verify-public.mjs
node scripts/release.mjs
node scripts/smoke-package.mjs
```

隔离测试使用合成临时数据，不需要真实用户配置或访问真实仓库。Windows 的符号链接测试取决于系统权限；若沙箱重写 junction 元数据，必须在正常 Windows 环境复核，不能通过移除安全断言宣称测试通过。原生宿主集成测试需单独配备支持的 Host，默认不访问真实 profile。

打包使用 npm 标准格式及显式文件白名单，并核对归档成员、字节和 SHA256。不上传任何备份，不执行 `npm publish`，不自动创建 GitHub Release。公开发布步骤及市场提交见 `PUBLISHING.md`，版本说明见 `CHANGELOG.md`。

plugins.description: Verification plugins for DeepSeek Harness - when the agent says it fixed something, these run it and hand you the evidence.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-verify

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-lightgrey.svg)](#limits)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen.svg)](package.json)

Your coding agent says "fixed it" after seeing a clean build. It has no way to know whether the fix
actually works — and neither do you, short of re-running everything yourself.

These plugins give it a way to find out, and to hand you something you can check.

```
agent:  "Fixed the config parser. Build is clean."

you:    verify_run(cmd: "build/app.exe")

        exit 0xC0000005   ACCESS_VIOLATION
        #0  parse_json    src/config.c:12    <- the line it just edited
        #1  load_config   src/config.c:22
        #2  main          src/main.c:34

agent:  "...it crashes. Looking again."
```

## Install

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile "$env:DSH_PROFILE" add @alexzeng666/dsh-verify
```

Windows x64. One package, twelve tools. The four sub-packages are its dependencies — installing
them separately double-registers their tools.

## The twelve

| | |
|---|---|
| **Run** | `verify_run` — exit code, stdout/stderr, and the stack when it crashes |
| **Assert** | `verify_assert_exit` · `verify_assert_stdout` · `verify_assert_file` · `verify_assert_json` · `verify_assert_screenshot` |
| **Report** | `verify_report` — folds the run history into one page |
| **Constrain** | `verify_limit` — CPU / memory / wall-clock caps; kills the whole job on overrun |
| **Explain** | `verify_attribution` — why it died: exit semantics, event log, minidump stack |
| **Inspect** | `verify_trace` — which APIs it called, with arguments |
| **Force** | `verify_hook` — override one API's return value (12-entry whitelist) |
| **Bend time** | `verify_timeshift` — speed up, slow down, or shift the target's clock |

## Evidence, not claims

Every run writes to `.verify/` in the workspace:

```
.verify/
  fragments.jsonl     one JSON line per verification
  timeline.jsonl      started / exited / killed / crashed / attached / shifted
  V-001.stdout.log
  V-001.stderr.log
  V-001.dmp           only when it crashed
```

`verify_report` reads them back. So "verified" becomes something you can audit next week, not a
sentence you have to take on faith.

## Why not just run the command

You can. For a build that exits 0 or 1, that is enough.

It stops being enough when:

- **The program crashes.** A shell gives you `exit code 1`. This gives you the frame and the
  source line.
- **The command hangs or eats the machine.** You get a cap and a clean kill instead of a dead
  session.
- **The conclusion is "the output contained X".** That is a claim, and claims need a record.

## Limits

- **Windows x64 only.** No 32-bit targets, no other platforms.
- **Native helpers ship prebuilt** — installing needs no compiler. Rebuilding them needs cmake
  plus mingw-w64; see [native/README.md](native/README.md).
- **`verify_hook` covers 12 fixed APIs.** Anything else is reported as unsupported rather than
  half-hooked.
- **Tracing a JIT runtime needs a narrower API set.** `verify_trace` hooks inline, and in node/V8
  hooking `QueryPerformanceCounter` terminates the process with `STATUS_BREAKPOINT`. Pass `apis`
  without it; every other API in the list is safe there.
- **The agent still has to call these tools.** A system-prompt rule nudges it to, but nothing
  forces it. What the tools guarantee is that when it *does* verify, the result is real.

## Packages

| Package | Provides |
|---|---|
| `dsh-verify` | run, assert, report — the umbrella |
| `dsh-quota` | `verify_limit` |
| `dsh-crashlab` | `verify_attribution` |
| `dsh-probe` | `verify_trace`, `verify_hook` |
| `dsh-timelab` | `verify_timeshift` |
| `dsh-verify-contract` | shared types; not published |

Each installs on its own. They couple only through
[`packages/dsh-verify-contract/src/index.d.ts`](packages/dsh-verify-contract/src/index.d.ts).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Bundled MinHook is BSD-2-Clause; see
[native/third_party/minhook/LICENSE.txt](native/third_party/minhook/LICENSE.txt).

plugins.description: dsh 三角色会话架构门禁 + manon 本地图谱组件（bundle：派遣规范门 / scout 常驻 / 地图前置 / 模型钉死 / 提交门 / 领导面限定 / manon 桥接）
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-verispring

Verispring three-role session architecture plus a bundled local knowledge graph (manon), substantially improving main-session context and reducing premium model API costs.
[中文](README.zh.md) | English

## What it enforces

| # | Gate | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dispatch spec gate | `subagent` / `subagent_fork` requires the dispatch spec content to have appeared in the session (a read result containing the spec's first-line marker; state is persisted in the session log and survives restarts) |
| 2 | Scout identity (dispatch intent) | The role is decided by the **`description` prefix the leader writes**: a dispatch whose description starts with `测绘智能体` or `scout` is a scout dispatch, anything else is an executor dispatch. Reachability only decides whether the dispatch may start, never the role: while a reachable scout exists, another scout dispatch is denied with a `send_message` reuse pointer (a scout waiting for a question showing finished/inactive is normal — `send_message` cold-resumes it); when no scout is reachable, an **executor dispatch is denied** with the `scout-missing` rule and three routes — `send_message` the previous scout, re-dispatch with a scout-prefixed description, or have the scout build/recheck the map first. It is never silently re-roled into a scout. Every scout dispatch gets a briefing (role, read-only duty, the unreachable previous scout, and the full repository map when present); only a successful scout start records `scoutId`, executor dispatches never touch that field. Child roles are persisted at spawn (`session-state/<child session id>.json`) and restored from the record, the session title, and the recorded scout id after reloads |
| 3 | Map first + baseline | Non-scout dispatch requires `<session workspace>/.project-map.md` (project root = `.git`/`.manon` present; otherwise fail-open); a `write`/`edit` of that file registers the current HEAD as the map baseline, and dispatch is denied while HEAD has advanced past it (the denial points to a scout incremental recheck plus a full `write` rewrite to re-register). A map without a registered baseline is denied too — no fail-open, so a stale map cannot stay valid forever. Fail-open only when `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` or HEAD cannot be read |
| 4 | Brief lint + executor cap | The executor brief is a result description, not a research request: briefs containing research wording (`BRIEF_LINT_TERMS` in `gates/dispatch-gate.js`) are denied with directions to `send_message` the scout instead — **negated mentions are exempt** (a negation within 6 characters before the hit, e.g. `不要通读实现` / `禁止先调研`). Running executors per leader session are capped (default 8); exceeding it is denied with "end the turn and wait for receipts". Both have kill switches (`CASEOS_BRIEF_LINT=0`, `CASEOS_MAX_EXECUTORS`) |
| 5 | Pinned model | Routes are enforced at runtime **per role**: a scout dispatch uses the panel's scout route, an executor dispatch the executor route (the role comes from the `description` prefix); explicit `provider`/`model` on the call is ignored. `subagent_fork` is always denied |
| 6 | Commit gate | `git commit` requires a prior read of `~/.dsh/specs/代码写作规范.md`; the shape is forced to `-F file -- explicit paths`, with `timeout`/`env`/`nice`/`nohup`/`stdbuf` style wrappers seen through |
| 7 | Leader scope | The leader's tool face shrinks to the review five (`bash`/`edit`/`write`/`read`/`read_image`) plus the dispatch face (`subagent`/`send_message`/`interrupt_agent`/`list_agents`/`release_subagent`), intersected with the tools that actually exist in the leader's view (desktop serves them from the preset layer, headless from the root layer); dispatch tools are shadowed by slim definitions, and those model-visible definitions are frozen per session (see "Per-session frozen tool surface"); `subagent-base` is unconditionally denied at the root layer (if the routing executor ever breaks, the model has no fallback to sneak through). Scout and executor subagents get the full face of the `verispring-subagent` preset; a scout's `edit`/`write` are hard-denied at runtime — `gates/dispatch-gate.js` matches the `scout` role from the queued dispatch plan on `agent/created` and calls `rtc.tools.restrict({ deny: ["edit", "write"] })` on the child's own scope, so the tools are absent from the scout's tool list (executors and the leader keep them). Kill switch `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` drops the scout part of the division clause and the restriction |
| 8 | Leader guard | Two kinds of runtime handling. **Denials (unchanged):** while a child is running, `sleep`/loop-waiting in `bash` is denied, and a second `list_agents` in the same turn is denied. **Hints (since 1.3.66):** `edit`/`write` outside the whitelist (`.project-map.md`, paths containing `/reports/`, `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md`, plus `CASEOS_LEADER_WRITE_ALLOW` prefixes) and `bash` change commands — `git commit/push/merge/rebase/restore/stash` (only `git stash list` / `git stash show` stay silent), `npm`/`pnpm` publish/install, `sed -i`/`perl -i`, `rm -rf`, workspace redirects — are **no longer denied**: the call runs as usual and one notice is appended after the tool result via the host `tools/post-execute` `additionalContexts` ("clear-boundary code and writing tasks go to an executor subagent; the leader does small fixes, the map, reports and verification writes"), at most once per turn, recorded to the monitor as `leader-write-hint` (rule + summary). Subagent sessions are unaffected. Kill switch `CASEOS_LEADER_GUARD=0` |
| 9 | Scout relay | The three loops that used to exist only in the prompt: `ask_scout` lets an executor hand a location/fact question to the resident scout and waits for the fresh answer (sender is the leader agent, since `sendMessage` authorizes by lineage; the answer is correlated by marker from the scout's session events, so a scout that settles right after answering still delivers it, and every wait round yields through a real ≥250 ms timer that is cleared when the wait ends); the closing "结构增量" (structure delta) section of a non-scout child is forwarded to the scout automatically; a failed child (`error`/`aborted`/`refusal`) writes a checkpoint that the plugin attaches when the leader continues it. Non-scout subagents get an injected ≤4-line locator discipline (`ask_scout` when a scout is reachable, "write it into your report" otherwise) plus the mandatory structure-delta section. Kill switch `CASEOS_SCOUT_RELAY=0`; `CASEOS_ASK_SCOUT_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds the wait |
| 10 | manon bridge | Resolves the local graph CLI (`MANON_KG_BIN` > bundled `manon/manon-kg` > legacy `~/manon/manon-kg`) and, when present, injects per role: the scout gets the full surface (commands, sourced invocation rule, ownership discipline), the leader gets one line ("graph facts come from the scout"), the executor gets one line — **manon is scout-owned; leader and executors never invoke it directly**; semantics in `~/.dsh/specs/Manon调用规则.md`. **The load-bearing part is the invocation rule**: dsh's subprocess service strips KEY/TOKEN-shaped env vars from children (anti-leak), so a bare `manon-kg sync` always fails with a missing key — the injected form sources `~/.dsh/manon.env` inside the bash command first (the scrub only strips the first hop; grandchildren inherit freely). Secret values never pass through or get printed |
| 11 | Secret hygiene | Credential/env files (`manon.env`, `verispring.env`, project `.env*`) cannot be read via `read` or echoed via `cat`/`sed` and friends (matched per command segment, so the sanctioned `source` prefix and pipes on manon output are not false positives); whole-environment dumps — bare `env`/`printenv`, `ps eww`, `/proc/*/environ`, `docker inspect` without `--format` — are denied |
| 12 | Runtime monitor | Role drift, gate denials, scout reachability changes and subagent start/end (role + route + stop reason, recorded only after a successful start) are appended to `~/.dsh/verispring-monitor.jsonl`, so audits no longer require decompressing session logs |

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CASEOS_SCOUT` | on | `0` drops the scout part of the division clause, t

**English** | [中文](#中文) --- ## 中文 设置页左侧那一列分区导航，插件装多了就变成一长条：顺序由各插件注册时写死、不能改，官方分区和一堆插件分区混在一起。这个插件给它加上**拖拽排序**和**自定义分组**，排布按浏览器保存，刷新不丢。 ### 功能 - **拖拽排序**：任意分区条目拖到任意位置，分组与普通条目混排也行。 - **分组**：把相关分区收进一个组（比如把「追问 / 通知 / 喵记忆」收成「系统增强」），点组头展开。 - **组内排序 / 跨组移动 / 拖出一级**：整理模式下组内条目同样能拖，可拖进别的组，也可拖回一级。 - **新建 / 重命名 / 删除分组**，同名会就地报错。 - **恢复默认**：一键清空排布，回到原生顺序（二次确认）。 - **两套视图**：平时收起成组头、点开是下拉菜单；点「整理导航」进整理模式，组内条目全部内联铺开，方便拖。 ### 效果图 日常使用：分组收起成一行，点开是带图标的浮动下拉菜单。 ![设置页导航：三个分组（模型提供 / 样式插件 / 系统增强）收起成一行，点开的「系统增强」下拉里列出追问、通知、喵记忆、bili 设置、备份与迁移、提示词优化设置、dsh-git-idea 配置，每项带原图标](assets/normal-mode.png) 整理模式：点右上角「整理导航」，组内条目全部铺开，可直接拖动排序。 ![整理模式：分组展开为小标题样式、成员条目内联缩进、行尾有 ⋮⋮ 拖拽把手与重命名/删除按钮，底部是「＋ 新建分组」与「恢复默认」](assets/edit-mode.png) ### 安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-settings-arranger ``` 装完刷新 Web GUI（或重启 dsh），bundle 会随包里的 `cordis.patch.yml` 自动注册。 > 用 GitHub 源安装：`dsh plugin --profile web add github:HelloQingTao/dsh-settings-arranger` ### 用法 1. 打开 **设置**，点右上角的 **整理导航**。 2. 点 **＋ 新建分组** 起个名字。 3. 把条目拖进组里，或把分组头拖到别的位置；组内条目可以再拖去别的组，或拖出一级。 4. 点 **完成** 退出整理模式，点分组头就能展开下拉菜单。 排布存在浏览器的 localStorage 里（键 `dsh.settings-arranger.v1`），**按浏览器与站点隔离**，换浏览器或换端口要重新整理。 ### 兼容 - dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` 实测通过。 - 纯客户端插件，只操作 DOM，不改任何其它插件的代码；同名的分区顺序仍由各插件自己的 `order` 决定，本插件只是在渲染后再重排。 ### 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE) --- ## English The settings dialog's left nav grows into an unmanageable list once you install a few plugins: order is baked in at registration time and official sections sit interleaved with plugin ones. This plugin adds **drag-to-reorder** and **custom groups**, persisted per browser. ### Features - **Drag to reorder** any section, mixing groups and plain rows freely. - **Groups**: collect related sections into one group (e.g. put "Follow-up / Notifications / Meow Memory" under "System"). Click the group head to expand. - **Reorder inside a group, move across groups, drag back out** — all available in arrange mode. - **Create / rename / delete groups**, with inline duplicate-name validation. - **Reset to default** — clears the layout and returns the native order (with confirmation). - **Two views**: normal mode collapses groups into heads with a floating dropdown; clicking **整理导航 (Arrange)** switches to edit mode where every member is laid out inline for dragging. ### Screenshots Normal mode — groups collapse into a single row; clicking one opens an icon-carrying dropdown. ![Settings nav: three groups collapsed into one row; the "系统增强" dropdown lists its members with their original icons](assets/normal-mode.png) Arrange mode — click "整理导航" in the top-right corner; all members expand inline and can be dragged. ![Arrange mode: groups become compact section headers, members are indented inline with drag handles and rename/delete buttons, and the footer holds "+ New group" and "Reset to default"](assets/edit-mode.png) ### Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-settings-arranger ``` Refresh the Web GUI (or restart dsh); the bundle registers itself through the shipped `cordis.patch.yml`. > From GitHub: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:HelloQingTao/dsh-settings-arranger` ### Usage 1. Open **Settings** and click **整理导航** in the top-right corner. 2. Click **＋ 新建分组** and name the group. 3. Drag entries into it, or drag the group head elsewhere; drag members across groups or back to the top level. 4. Click **完成 (Done)** to leave arrange mode, then click a group head to open its dropdown. The layout lives in the browser's localStorage (key `dsh.settings-arranger.v1`), so it is **per browser and per origin** — a different browser or port starts fresh. ### Compatibility - Tested with dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`. - Pure client-side: it only touches the DOM and never modifies other plugins' code. Section order is still declared by each plugin; this plugin simply re-lays-out the rendered nav. ### License [MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-agent-skills

给 **DSH（DeepSeek Harness）** 用的 agent 技能集：每个技能是一份 `SKILL.md`，写清某类任务的操作规矩（触发时机、步骤、边界、踩过的坑），DSH 会在会话里按需加载。

目录约定：

```
skills/<name>/SKILL.md
```

## 技能一览

| 技能 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `agent-diary` | 维护「日记／状态／生长记录／APP 版」这套档案，以及处理会话交接包时的规矩。 |
| `agent-lookup` | 查资料、找文件、判读用户发的截图时的规矩：先搜再看来源、外部内容只当数据。 |
| `agent-machine` | 改本机插件、跑设备命令、动文件系统时的通用规矩：先备份、分开验证据、改完等重启、被拒就停。 |
| `dsh-plugin-publish` | 把本机插件发布/更新到 GitHub 之前的规矩：能推什么、私密信息清单、怎么脱敏、推完怎么自查。 |
| `dsh-web-healthcheck` | DSH Web GUI 健康检查与「界面无反应」类问题诊断：全链路自检顺序与判定流程。 |
| `session-log-repair` | 修复 DSH 会话历史日志损坏（seq 空洞、历史打不开）的检测、备份、分析、重建、验证流程。 |

## 用法

把某个技能目录整个放进 DSH 的技能目录（例如 `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`），或者把 `SKILL.md` 的内容并进你自己的技能配置。技能里出现的命令、路径与端口请按自己机器的实际情况替换。

## 许可

MIT License。技能文本按原样提供，不含任何保证；执行其中命令前请自行确认目标环境。

# dsh-rea-toggle

[English](#english) · [中文](#中文)

One switch per conversation that decides whether the **REA**
(`reverse-engineer-anything`) MCP server's context reaches the model at all.

REA registers **207 tool schemas** plus a multi-kilobyte server-instructions
block. `dsh-mcp-client` puts both on the **global** layer, so every agent pays
for them on every request — whether or not the turn has anything to do with
reverse engineering.

With this plugin installed, a small pill appears below the composer:

- **REA on** (green) — exactly the pre-install behaviour. REA's tools and
  instructions are visible to the model.
- **REA off** (grey) — those 207 tool schemas and the `mcp:rea` instructions
  block **leave the model context**, taking effect on the next step.

**The switch is per conversation.** Each conversation remembers its own
position, and a new conversation starts **off**. That is the whole point: a
conversation about a web app should not pay for 207 reverse-engineering schemas
just because some other conversation needs them. Subagents inherit the position
of the conversation that created them, so delegating inside reverse-engineering
work does not silently break the subagent.

The same switch is on the keyboard: `/rea off`, `/rea on`, `/rea status`,
`/rea toggle` — all acting on the conversation you typed them in.

Nothing is uninstalled and nothing restarts. The MCP connection stays up; the
model simply stops being told those tools exist.

---

## English

### What it actually does

The token cost comes from two different places that travel two different paths,
so one mechanism is not enough:

| Target | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Tool schemas | `tools.restrict({ deny })` is called **in each agent's own context**. `ToolRuntime.view()` filters what that scope *inherits* from the global layer, and the model-facing schema list is rebuilt from that view on every assembly. The reserved `run_code` transport sits outside the filterable layers, so it is unaffected. |
| Instructions text | `dsh-mcp-client` registers the server instructions as a prompt section named `mcp:<server>` at order `MCP_SERVERS` (3100). **A scoped section with the same name shadows the global one** — a documented contract of `systemPrompt.section()` ("a scoped section shadows a global section with the same name"), not an implementation detail — and an empty section is dropped at render (`renderPrompt` keeps only `text.length > 0`). Registering that name and returning `''` therefore removes the block for that agent alone. |

Both are scoped registrations, so disposing them restores the previous state
exactly. That is why flipping the switch needs no restart and no reload.

Coverage includes **subagents**: `agent/created` is serial and awaited by the
registry, so installing inside it lands ahead of any prompt assembly.

### Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:aurumple/dsh-rea-toggle
```

Or point at a checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-rea-toggle
```

The bundle row id is `rea-toggle`; the package name is `dsh-rea-toggle`.

### Use

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| Pill under the composer | Click to flip **this conversation**. Green = on, grey = off, red border = the host did not answer. |
| `/rea off` · `/rea on` | Set this conversation's position. `enable` / `disable` work too. |
| `/rea toggle` | Flip this conversation. |
| `/rea status` | Report this conversation's position. |

A new conversation starts off. The first time you turn one on, that conversation
is remembered; conversations you never touch stay on the default and are not
written down.

Positions are remembered in `$DSH_HOME/rea-toggle.json` (usually
`~/.dsh/rea-toggle.json`), keyed by session id, and survive a restart. The file
keeps the 500 most recently changed conversations; an older one simply falls
back to the default.

### Configuration

Every field is optional.

```yaml
- id: rea-toggle
  name: dsh-rea-toggle
  config:
    server: rea               # one MCP server to govern; default "rea"
    # servers: [rea, ghidra]  # or several; wins over `server` when present
    # defaultEnabled: true    # new conversations start ON instead of off
```

Changing `server` governs a different MCP server by the same rules: tool prefix
`mcp__<server>__`, instructions section `mcp:<server>`. Because the mechanism is
generic, this works for any MCP server whose tools are bridged by
`dsh-mcp-client` — the REA case is just the one that motivated it.

`defaultEnabled` exists for anyone who wants the pre-plugin behaviour back: with
it on, a conversation nobody has switched behaves exactly as if this plugin were
not installed.

### HTTP API

The Client half talks to the Host over one exact route on the bare `webServer`
(the same shape other bundles use, so it does not travel through the `/api`
prefix fence). The conversation is `session=` on GET and a body field on POST:
the pill always knows which conversation it is showing, and a request that does
not say cannot be answered for it.

```
GET  /rea-toggle/state?session=<id>
  -> { session, enabled, known, defaultEnabled, servers, agents, tools, statePath }

GET  /rea-toggle/state            (no session: a summary)
  -> { session: null, defaultEnabled, servers, conversations, agents, tools, statePath }

POST /rea-toggle/state
  body: { "session": "<id>", "enabled": true | false }   (omit `enabled` to flip)
  -> the per-conversation status object
```

`known` says whether this conversation has ever been switched; when it is
`false`, `enabled` is just `defaultEnabled` and nothing has been written yet.
`agents` is how many live agents of that conversation are currently covered;
`tools` is how many of the governed server's tools were recognised, which is the
honest answer to "did it find REA at all" — if it reads `0`, the server is not
connected under that name (and stays `0`-safe because `restrictableNames` is the
denyable set, not the filtered view).

### Scope and limits

- **One server per row by default.** Other MCP servers are untouched; use
  `servers` to govern more than one.
- **Hidden, not unloaded.** The MCP connection stays up and the REA process
  keeps running. When the switch is off the model simply cannot reach it —
  including indirectly through `run_code`. That is deliberate: leaving a second
  path open would save only half the tokens.
- **Per-conversation state, in-process.** Positions are read from the file at
  `apply()` and written on every change. Two DSH instances sharing one profile
  each read it once and do not live-sync with each other.
- **It does not delete anything.** Turning it off is reversible in one click,
  and uninstalling the bundle lifts every registration.

### Verify it yourself

The claim is that the tools are gone from the model's context, not merely
hidden in a UI. Check it where the model's own view is exposed:

1. With the switch **on**, ask the agent to list its tools — `mcp__rea__*`
   entries are there (207 of them for a stock REA install).
2. Turn it **off**, ask again — they are gone, and calling one by name returns
   `Error: unknown tool "mcp__rea__binary_session"`.
3. Turn it back **on** — they return, unchanged.
4. Open a **second conversation** and check its tool list: it is off, while the
   first one is still on. That is the property that distinguishes this plugin
   from a global toggle.

### Development

```bash
npm test        # node:test, no dependencies
```

The suite drives the real `apply()` against a small model of the three
contracts it depends on (tool view, prompt section merge, agent registry). It
pins what "off" removes, that "on" restores the previous state exactly, that a
new subagent is covered before its first step, that the position survives a
restart, and that the HTTP surface validates its input.

### License

MIT

---

## 中文

一个开关（**每个对话一个**），决定 **REA**（`reverse-engineer-anything`）MCP
服务器的上下文是否进入模型。

REA 注册了 **207 个工具 schema**，外加一段几千字的服务端说明。
`dsh-mcp-client` 把它们放在**全局层**，所以每个 agent、每次请求都在为它们付
token —— 不管这一轮到底要不要逆向。

装上这个插件后，聊天输入框下方会多一个小胶囊：

- **REA 开**（绿色）— 和装之前完全一样，REA 的工具与说明对模型可见。
- **REA 关**（灰色）— 这 207 个工具 schema 和

plugins.description: Unofficial visual control panel and MCP bridge for DeepSeek Harness: model, workspace and permission controls, task monitoring, and reusable sessions.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-bridge

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**A visible control panel for Claude Code and Codex delegation to DeepSeek Harness.** Choose the model, provider, workspace, and new-session permissions in Harness; inspect task state through MCP; find and continue the resulting conversations.

This project is for people who want to spend less of their main model's effort on bounded supporting tasks, and make repeated Harness calls and the resulting sessions easier to manage.

> Third-party, unofficial integration. Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek, Anthropic, or OpenAI. Harness interfaces and MCP clients can change; check the compatibility notes before upgrading.

> **Archive-only maintenance in 0.2.4:** permanent deletion is disabled in every plugin entry point. The compatible `autoCleanupDays` setting now archives eligible MCP-created sessions, keeps their files, and uses the official non-stopping option; `0` turns automatic archival off. Old pending-delete files are retained unchanged and never executed. See [maintenance boundaries and upgrade notes](docs/troubleshooting.md#cleanup-limitation-and-pending-deletions).

## Why this bridge?

- **Delegate selectively.** Send a narrow review, summary, documentation task, or investigation to Harness, then bring the result back to your main agent.
- **Keep responsibility clear.** The main agent still scopes the task, checks the result, and integrates useful work.
- **Keep controls visible.** Use Harness's toolbar for task constraints and its conversations for context; use MCP status/results to inspect execution rather than relying on a silent handoff.
- **Manage repeated delegation.** Find task IDs after a disconnect, continue managed sessions, and archive conversations you want to keep.

Delegation can reduce the amount of work the main model performs, but it does not guarantee a fixed quota reduction, lower total cost, or faster completion. DeepSeek or your chosen provider can still charge for delegated work, and coordination, retries, and review still consume resources. See [choosing and measuring delegated tasks](docs/delegation.md).

## How it fits together

1. Claude Code, Codex, or another compatible MCP client sends a tool request.
2. The local bridge connects that request to the plugin running in DeepSeek Harness.
3. A Harness agent uses the configured provider, workspace, and execution permissions.
4. The client receives the task result for review and further work.

**A local bridge does not mean local model inference.** Prompts and relevant workspace content may be sent to the provider configured in Harness. Check your provider's terms and your own data-sharing permissions before delegating private material.

The current plugin installs into the **desktop profile**, so that Harness host must be running. This is a good fit if you already use Harness and delegate frequently. A one-off task may not justify the extra installation and process. Harness also has an official CLI; other hosting profiles for this plugin have not been verified. [CLI and hosting FAQ](docs/troubleshooting.md#does-harness-have-a-cli).

## Quick start

Bridge version: **0.2.4**. Target Harness desktop version: **0.2.1-rc.2**. Build with Node.js **22+** and npm. Maintainer-provided verification notes cover Windows; they do not establish support for every platform or MCP client.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FishCityBee/dsh-mcp-bridge.git
cd dsh-mcp-bridge
npm ci
npm run build
```

Install `dist-package/` with Harness's bundled CLI. Windows PowerShell example, with paths replaced for your installation:

```powershell
& "D:\Program Files\Deepseek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add "C:\path\to\dsh-mcp-bridge\dist-package"
```

Completely quit Harness, including the tray process, and reopen it. In the bridge toolbar, select your provider/model, a disposable default workspace, and read-only new-session permissions. Automatic archival defaults to off; enable it only after reviewing its scope.

Register the relay in the client you use, with its absolute path:

```sh
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user dsh-harness -- node "C:/path/to/dsh-mcp-bridge/dist-package/bin/stdio.mjs"

# Codex
codex mcp add dsh-harness -- node "C:/path/to/dsh-mcp-bridge/dist-package/bin/stdio.mjs"
```

Ask the client to call `harness_status`, `list_models`, and `list_workspaces` before starting a task. Then try one small task with no file changes. Model tasks can incur provider charges. See [installation, timeouts, environment variables, and upgrade steps](docs/installation.md) for complete instructions and official client references.

## Controls that matter

- **Model constraints:** single-model mode locks provider/model/effort. Provider mode also locks model/effort unless the user enables caller overrides; the provider stays locked.
- **Execution evidence:** requested and effective model selections are separate. `effectiveSelection` is populated only after the bridge observes a request, and does not prove provider acceptance or billing.
- **Permissions:** new-session presets use Harness's official permission service; that selector leaves existing sessions unchanged. Full access is a high-risk option, not a setup requirement.
- **Task lifecycle:** start, wait, inspect, find, and cancel tasks. Client disconnects are separate from task cancellation; cancellation cannot undo completed effects.
- **Sessions:** continue bridge-managed conversations and archive/unarchive them. Automatic maintenance only archives; permanent deletion is unavailable.

The default connection uses a local pipe/socket with the stdio relay, without opening a TCP port. Optional HTTP is off by default. Update the plugin and the entire relay together; 0.2.4 uses `tls-pinned-v3` and does not fall back to older handshakes.

## Documentation

- [Installation and Claude Code / Codex setup](docs/installation.md)
- [Configuration, model defaults, and permission boundaries](docs/configuration.md)
- [Tool reference, task recovery, and session maintenance](docs/usage.md)
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](docs/troubleshooting.md)
- [Delegating useful work](docs/delegation.md)
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Security and responsible reporting](SECURITY.md)

## Permission boundaries

There are two separate decisions: whether your MCP client may call a bridge tool, and whether the Harness agent may perform an operation. Client-side MCP approval is not a replacement for Harness execution approval. Choosing a workspace does not by itself sandbox an agent.

Start in a disposable workspace with a small, read-only task. Keep credentials out of prompts, screenshots, and issue reports. Review substantive results before accepting changes. Back up important session data. Plugin deletion stays disabled until an official safe cross-process deletion boundary is available.

## Compatibility and verification

This bridge relies on version-specific Harness APIs and storage behavior. Other Harness versions, alternate profiles, and all client/platform combinations are not implied to be supported.

The repository includes maintainer-written technical records in Chinese: [reliability changes](docs/audit-2026-10-17.md), [desktop transport checks](docs/desktop-2026-10-18.md), and [new-session permission checks](docs/ui-permissions-2026-10-18.md). The [0.2.4 maintenance notes](docs/recheck-0.2.4.md) distinguish the current changes from earlier historical reports. Their stated test scope and remaining gaps matter; they are not a claim that all security risks or UI paths have been validated.

## Contribute

Bug reports, compatibility checks, translations, and focused pull requests are welcome in English or Chinese. Please read the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md), and keep secrets and private session content out of public reports.

If this project helps your workflow, a star helps others discover it.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The existing copyright and license notices apply.

plugins.readme_text:
SVG Studio

Image + prompt → pure, layered SVG.
A local-first vectorization studio for DeepSeek Harness.
Built and maintained by xiangwriter.

dsh-xiangwriter-svg-studio

简体中文 · Install · Usage · Engine · Development · License

> **Personal, non-commercial use only.** > This repository is source-available, not open-source. Commercial use of any kind > requires a separate written licence from xiangwriter; see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md). > The `xiangwriter` name, mark and branding must remain intact. --- SVG Studio turns a character illustration, sticker or flat-colour image into a **real SVG made of paths, gradients and masks** — no embedded bitmap, no external tracing service. It ships as three things in one DeepSeek Harness plugin: - a full **Web Studio** page in the Harness sidebar, - an agent tool, **`svg_studio`**, for file-path workflows, - a reusable agent skill, **`svg-vector-recreation`**. Everything runs locally. Images and prompts go only to the local Harness server and the local Python engine. ## Why it exists Most image-to-SVG tools either return one giant traced path, or quietly embed the source PNG inside an SVG. SVG Studio is built for character art: it keeps the figure, refines the face locally, builds a clean backdrop, and validates that the result is genuinely vector. The original illustration is never included in this repository; the plugin contains code and synthetic test fixtures only. ## Highlights - **Prompt-guided presets.** Write what you want in natural language (“keep the wine-red backdrop, clean up the contour, more detail in the eyes”) and the engine maps those notes to colour counts, face detail and backdrop settings. Explicit overrides always win. - **Layered colour tracing.** Median-cut palette → connected colour regions → closed contours with even-odd holes → optional RDP simplification. A single colour can contain many islands. - **A figure-aware clip.** The engine samples the backdrop, separates it from the figure, handles interior holes and near-white areas, then pre-clips colour paths to the character. Background noise and stray colour blobs are less likely to become paths. - **Local face-detail pass.** A small, soft-masked palette refines eyes, cheeks, mouth and hair details without changing the rest of the image. - **Clean backdrops without invented effects.** The default `gradient` backdrop is a clean gradient derived from the source border. It does **not** add a synthetic halo or dark ring. Choose `original` to keep the source background. - **Outline is opt-in.** The extra dark outer contour is **off by default**. Turn it on in Advanced settings only when you want a sticker-like rim. - **Small, inspectable output.** Paths, gradients, a soft face mask, and no `` or `data:image` payloads. A structural check rejects malformed SVG. - **Bounded work.** Long edges above 1200 px are scaled down; the engine warns when an output gets large. Typical 240 px chibi art completes in under two seconds. - **English and Chinese UI**, with locale files you can extend. ## Install Requires a DeepSeek Harness profile with the Web UI and a Python 3.10+ interpreter with **Pillow** and **numpy**. 1. Install the plugin from GitHub: ```bash dsh plugin add github:xiangwriter-dev/dsh-xiangwriter-svg-studio ``` Or from a local checkout: ```bash dsh plugin add /absolute/path/to/dsh-xiangwriter-svg-studio ``` 2. Install the Python engine dependencies into the interpreter DSH can see: ```bash python -m pip install -r engine/requirements.txt ``` On Windows, DSH also detects its bundled Python runtime and `DSH_SVG_STUDIO_PYTHON` if set. The Studio page shows **Local engine ready** when Pillow and numpy are available. 3. Refresh the Harness Web UI. The sidebar entry **SVG Studio / SVG 矢量化** opens the Studio. The plugin is a bundle with a Host half (`index.js`), a Web client (`client.js`), a Cordis patch, locale metadata and the Python engine. ## Use it ### In the Web Studio 1. Drop a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF, or click to choose one. Images are normalised to a maximum 1200 px long edge and flattened onto white before upload. 2. Optional: write a short direction in **Your ideas and direction**. 3. Pick a preset (or open **Advanced settings**). 4. Press **Generate SVG**. Preview, download, copy the code, or open the SVG in a new tab. ### From an agent Ask in natural language; the skill is selected automatically when the task matches it: ```text Use svg_studio on D:\art\character.png. Preset: faithful. Keep face detail on, outer contour off, clean gradient background. Save the SVG next to the source. ``` Or call the tool directly. Common arguments: | Argument | Values | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `image_path` | local path | PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF | | `prompt` | free text | Stored in the SVG description; guides settings | | `preset` | `faithful`, `clean`, `flat`, `original`, `mini` | Defaults to `faithful` | | `colors` | 24–224 | Overrides the preset palette size | | `face_detail` | boolean | Local face pass | | `outline` | boolean | Extra outer rim, off by default | | `background` | `auto`, `gradient`, `original` | Clean gradient, auto, or source backdrop | | `saturation`, `contrast` | numbers | Small colour adjustments | | `output_path` | local path | Optional destination for the `.svg` | ### Presets | Preset | Palette | Face pass | Backdrop | Best for | | --- | ---: | :---: | --- | --- | | `faithful` | 160 | on | clean gradient | closest overall recreation | | `clean` | 112 | on | clean gradient | smaller, flatter, tidier files | | `flat` | 72 | off | clean gradient | poster-like colour masses | | `original` | 140 | on | source backdrop | scenes, photos, or when the backdrop is part of the art | | `mini` | 64 | off | clean gradient | very simple art and tiny files | The outer contour is independent of the preset and is **off by default**. ## Output contract - The SVG contains ``, ``, ``, ``, `` and a `` — no raster image. - The output is XML-validated; ``, `data:image`, and base64 payloads are rejected. - Generated files are stored under `$DSH_HOME/svg-studio/outputs/` and pruned to the newest 40. - The result is a local file; nothing is uploaded to a cloud service. ## Local API The Studio talks to three exact, local-only routes served by the Host plugin: | Method | Route | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `GET` | `/svg-studio/api/health` | Python, Pillow and numpy availability | | `POST` | `/svg-studio/api/generate` | data-URL or file-path generation | | `GET` | `/svg-studio/file?name=.svg` | serve a saved output from the output directory | These routes are registered on the local Harness web server and are not intended to be exposed publicly. ## How the engine works ```text source image │ normalize / flatten ▼ adaptive palette

plugins.description: Bring Headroom to your DeepSeek Harness as a native plugin.
plugins.readme_text:
# DeepSeek-Harness-Headroom-Plugin

![bundle](https://img.shields.io/badge/bundle-v1.0.1-CB3837?logo=npm&logoColor=white)
![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-brightgreen)
![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek_Harness-plugin-4D6BFE?logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)

Bring [Headroom](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom) — a local-first
context-compression toolkit — to the **DeepSeek Harness** as a native plugin.

After installing, your DSH can compress large blobs on demand and retrieve the
originals byte-for-byte, and any provider you point at the bundled proxy gets
compressed transparently — no changes to your prompts.

**[中文文档](README.zh.md)**

---

## What you get

Three native tools, exposed through Headroom's own MCP server:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_compress` | Compress a large blob (tool output, file, log, search result) → compressed text + a retrieval hash |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_retrieve` | Fetch the byte-identical original back by that hash |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_stats` | Session stats: compressions, tokens saved, estimated cost |

Two ways to use them, and they are independent:

**1. On-demand tools — works with any provider.** The model decides when to call
them. Nothing about your traffic changes; you gain compression only when the agent
chooses to use it.

**2. Transparent compression — an HTTP proxy.** Every byte of traffic through a
repointed provider is compressed automatically, whether or not the model asks.
Measured on a 500-row tool result:

```
before    : 27665 tokens
after     : 18812 tokens
saved     :  8853 tokens  (32.0%)
transform : router:smart_crusher:0.54
```

The FATAL row (id 67) survived compression, and the model still answered with it.
Compression is **reversible**: originals live in a local store and come back
byte-identical, so nothing is lost — it is only deferred. Byte-identity is a
property of the *store*, not of the compacted text: what the model reads inline is
lossy, and the original is recovered by asking for it.

## Install

**Prerequisites:** a working DSH profile, and `uv`/`uvx` on `PATH`.

If `uvx --version` does not print a version yet, install `uv` first — it is the one
prerequisite, and the same command works on Windows, macOS and Linux:

```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# or, if you already have Python and pip
pip install uv
```

Reopen the terminal afterwards and check `uvx --version`. Nothing else is
required: `uvx` fetches Headroom and all of its Python dependencies by itself,
so there is no Python environment to create and no package to build.

Clone this repository anywhere you like — the MCP row starts `uvx` from `PATH`, so
it does not care where the bundle is installed; only the `install_bundle` step
needs an absolute path to locate the bundle.

```bash
git clone <this-repo> dsh-headroom
cd dsh-headroom
```

Nothing needs building. Headroom itself is fetched by `uvx` on first use, and the
proxy environment is created on demand by its launcher.

### Step 1 — nothing to configure

The shipped patch is zero-config — it pulls up the upstream `headroom mcp serve`
directly via `uvx` on `PATH`, so there is nothing to edit:

```yaml
command: uvx
args:
  - '--from'
  - 'headroom-ai[mcp]'
  - 'headroom'
  - 'mcp'
  - 'serve'
env:
  HEADROOM_BEACON: 'off'
  HEADROOM_UPDATE_CHECK: 'off'
  HEADROOM_TIKTOKEN_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '120'
failOnStartupError: true
```

`command` has no directory component, and the stdio transport resolves it through
the `PATH` (`cross-spawn`), so neither the install location nor the Host's working
directory matters any more — which is exactly what makes a config-only patch
portable. `uvx` is the same name on Windows (`uvx.exe`), macOS, and Linux, so the
MCP row has no `.cmd`/`.sh` platform split. `args` reaches the child as the argv
verbatim, so `headroom-ai[mcp]` needs no quoting.

### Step 2 — install the bundle

```
plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=<absolute-path-to-this-repo>\plugin
```

That runs `pnpm` in your profile, links `@local/dsh-headroom` into
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules`, and applies the patch to the live
profile. Success reports `application: applied` with empty `warnings`. Restart
DSH if your profile is not the live one. Once installed, the `headroom-mcp` row is
`active` and the three `mcp__headroom__*` tools are immediately usable — no need
to launch the Harness from any particular directory.

> This one path is unavoidably absolute — `install_bundle` is told *where the
> bundle is* by you. Everything after it is relative.

### Step 3 — remove it again

```
plugin_manager  action=remove_bundle  target=@local/dsh-headroom
```

### A note on environment variables

DSH scrubs the environment it hands to MCP children: any name matching
`/KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i` is dropped, as is any name beginning with `DSH_`
(`dsh-subprocess/lib/index.js:32,52`). This bundle's variables are all named
`HEADROOM_*`, so they pass through untouched — but it is worth knowing before you
add a credential-style name of your own.

`HEADROOM_DSH_WORKSPACE` overrides the launchers' workspace detection. You only
need it if you invoke a launcher from a relocated or symlinked location.

## Verifying the install

[`plugin/verify/verify_headroom.py`](plugin/verify/verify_headroom.py) proves the
whole chain end-to-end — the sanitizer, model discovery, a real SSE stream, and
an actual compression:

```
.proxy-venv/Scripts/python.exe plugin/verify/verify_headroom.py \
    --credentials ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml
```

```
==========================================================================
summary
==========================================================================
  header     PASS
  discovery  PASS
  stream     PASS
  compress   PASS

OVERALL: PASS
```

Each check prints its own `RESULT: PASS` line with the numbers it observed, so a
failing run says which stage failed and why. `--only header` runs the offline
check that needs no key and no network. Exit code is non-zero on failure, so it
drops straight into CI.

[`plugin/README.md`](plugin/README.md) additionally documents the MCP handshake
check and the other manual verification steps.

## Transparent compression (the proxy)

Start the proxy — **nothing auto-starts it**, and it needs to be told where to
forward:

```powershell
plugin\bin\headroom-proxy.cmd https://your-provider.example/v1
```

There is deliberately **no built-in upstream**. A proxy that silently forwarded to
an endpoint you did not choose would send your content and your API key somewhere
unexpected, so the launcher exits with an error instead of guessing. Give it an
argument, `HEADROOM_UPSTREAM_URL`, or a pre-existing `OPENAI_TARGET_API_URL`.

Then point a provider's `baseURL` at it:

```yaml
# your profile's cordis.patch.yml, inside an llm-pi-ai provider
baseURL: http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1
```

The proxy forwards to `OPENAI_TARGET_API_URL` and passes the client's
`Authorization` header through unchanged, so the provider key stays whatever DSH
already sends — nothing is duplicated, intercepted, or stored. Per-request token
accounting appears in the response headers (`x-headroom-tokens-before/after/saved`,
`x-headroom-transforms`), and running totals land in
`.headroom/savings_events.jsonl`.

Three settings matter, and all three were necessary here:

| Setting | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode` | `token` | `cache` mode freezes prior turns to protect the provider's prefix cache; a frozen payload is never compressed, which measured **zero** savings. `token` mode does not freeze. Both modes behave identically on content neither one freezes. |
| `HEADROOM_HF_TOKENIZER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `0` | The HF tokenizer download never completes here, so every request stalled for the full timeout (~10s). Disabling the fetch cut `opt_ms` from ~10000ms to 26–66ms. |
| A patched venv | via `bin/setup-proxy

plugins.description: Background-first macOS cross-application desktop tools for DeepSeek Harness, with hidden agent cursor and post-action observations.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Computer Use Next

macOS 全局跨应用桌面控制插件。默认隐藏虚拟光标，在后台选定窗口；窗口操作后自动回读界面，供 DSH 模型继续判断。

基于 MIT 授权的 [dsh-computer-use 0.3.1](https://github.com/988hj7tczd-oss/dsh-computer-use) 修改，保留原许可，变更见 NOTICE。本项目与 OpenAI、Codex 无隶属关系，不包含其内部实现或模型。

## 要求

- macOS；其他操作系统未验证。
- Node.js 22.18+；兼容 @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools 0.2.0-rc.2 接口的 DSH 宿主。
- 已安装 CuaDriver，并授予其辅助功能和屏幕录制权限；实测版本 0.35.2。
- 原生图片和整屏观察需要对话模型支持图片输入，否则使用窗口 AX 控件树。

## 安装

发布后可通过 GitHub Release 中的 dsh-computer-use-next.tgz 安装，或由收录后的 DSH 插件市场安装。仓库自带 dsh.bundle manifest 和运行时 JavaScript，不需要编译。

本机桌面 profile 的手动安装：

```sh
python3 install.py
```

脚本只针对已有 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop 的桌面版，复制插件、备份并追加配置，不重启应用、不更改模型账号。其他 profile 使用宿主的插件安装方式。

如已启用旧版 dsh-computer-use，先禁用旧版，避免同名工具重复注册；本插件不会擅自禁用其他插件。

## 工具

| 工具 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| desktop_windows | 全局应用窗口列表及精确窗口 ID。 |
| app_switch | 后台选定并观察目标窗口，不主动前置。 |
| desktop_observe | 主显示器整屏图片，包括 Dock 和菜单栏。 |
| desktop_click | 全局坐标点击及回读；后台模式默认禁用。 |
| screen_observe | 窗口 AX 控件树及可用截图。 |
| screen_zoom | 局部截图。 |
| computer_click / computer_double_click / computer_right_click | 窗口点击、双击、右键。 |
| computer_type / computer_key | 目标窗口文本输入及快捷键。 |
| computer_scroll / computer_drag | 窗口内滚动及拖拽。 |
| computer_wait | 等待加载。 |
| app_list / app_launch | 应用列表及启动。 |

合计 16 个工具。窗口点击、输入、按键、滚动和拖拽后自动回读原窗口，模型需要检查实际变化。不同 agent 的观察缓存隔离，插件内调用串行执行。

示例：

> 使用 desktop_windows 查看窗口，选定计算器计算 12+34，再观察另一个应用，最后回到计算器核对结果。保持后台，每步检查界面，不重复执行结果未知的动作。

## 后台与前台

默认 backgroundOnly=true、animateCursor=false。驱动会话初始化和恢复时关闭虚拟光标，不隐藏用户自己的鼠标。

后台模式禁止主动前置及 desktop_click；使用 app_launch 和 app_switch 跨应用工作。不支持后台的操作会失败，不自动前置重试；应用自身弹窗仍可能改变焦点，不能保证所有软件完全后台运行。

如需 Dock/菜单栏点击，可显式设置 backgroundOnly=false，允许前台交互。整屏坐标和窗口坐标不能混用。

未验证多屏、其他 Space、最小化窗口及完整模型驱动的跨应用长任务；未实现跨窗口拖拽、视频流或独立无人值守规划。

## 数据和权限

截图经 DSH attachments 服务处理，可能按模型路由发送给模型服务商。显式 vision 模式继承上游观察者及可选 GLM fallback，其密钥查找和请求见 lib/vision.js。默认 native/AX 路径不新增密钥。

快照 TTL、应用白名单和部分按钮审批规则不是完整安全保障，坐标点击及快捷键不能可靠推断业务后果。详见 PERMISSIONS.md。

## 验证和卸载

```sh
node --test tests/*.test.mjs
python3 install.py --uninstall
```

16 项自动测试通过。实际验证了计算器点击与截图回读、计算器与 DSH 的后台窗口观察、1568×1014 整屏读取及虚拟光标关闭。完整模型任务尚未验证。

卸载只移除本插件的配置块，保留其他配置及插件文件。下一次启动或宿主重新加载配置后生效。
